title: Implement glob-style pattern matching in Go
description: Greenfield Go task: implement Match(pattern, text string) bool using DP. '*' matches any sequence (including empty), '?' matches exactly one character, all other chars match literally.

task_spec.prompt:
Implement glob-style pattern matching in glob.go.

func Match(pattern, text string) bool
  // '*' matches any sequence of characters (including empty).
  // '?' matches exactly one character.
  // All other characters match literally.

Recommended approach: 2D DP table dp[i][j] = pattern[:i] matches text[:j].
  - dp[0][0] = true
  - dp[i][0] = true if pattern[:i] is all '*'
  - dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1] if pattern[i-1] matches text[j-1] (literal or ?)
  - dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j] || dp[i][j-1] if pattern[i-1] == '*'

All 5 tests in glob_test.go must pass.
Run: go test ./...
required_artifacts: Base case: dp[0][0]=true, dp[i][0]=true while pattern[i-1]=='*'
Literal/? case: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1] && (pattern[i-1]=='?' || chars match)
followup_prompts: Run `go test ./...` and show me which tests are passing and which are still failing. Fix any failures — pay attention to edge cases like empty input, boundary values, and error conditions.
Final check: run `go test ./...` one more time. All tests must be green. If anything is still failing, trace through the failing assertion and fix it now.
